claim: Mutations in the human telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter are the most frequent non-coding mutations in cancer.
source: Mutations in the human telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter are the most frequent non-coding mutations in cancer, but their molecular mechanism in tumorigenesis has not been established.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature establishing the frequency of TERT promoter mutations in cancer.

claim: Telomerase-expressing embryonic stem cells engineered to carry any of the three most frequent TERT promoter mutations showed only a modest increase in TERT transcription with no impact on telomerase activity.
source: Surprisingly, telomerase-expressing embryonic stem cells engineered to carry any of the three most frequent TERT promoter mutations showed only a modest increase in TERT transcription with no impact on telomerase activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, including qRT-PCR and TRAP assays shown in Figure 1.

claim: Upon differentiation into somatic cells, cells with TERT promoter mutations failed to silence TERT expression, resulting in increased telomerase activity and aberrantly long telomeres.
source: However, upon differentiation into somatic cells, which normally silence telomerase, cells with TERT promoter mutations failed to silence TERT expression, resulting in increased telomerase activity and aberrantly long telomeres.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data including qRT-PCR, TRAP assays, and telomere length measurements shown in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: TERT promoter mutations are sufficient to overcome the proliferative barrier imposed by telomere shortening without additional tumor-selected mutations.
source: Thus, TERT promoter mutations are sufficient to overcome the proliferative barrier imposed by telomere shortening without additional tumor-selected mutations.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that cells with TERT promoter mutations maintain telomere length in differentiated cells and teratomas.

claim: TERT promoter mutations can promote immortalization and tumorigenesis of incipient cancer cells.
source: These data establish that TERT promoter mutations can promote immortalization and tumorigenesis of incipient cancer cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing sustained telomerase activity and telomere maintenance in differentiated cells with TERT promoter mutations.

claim: Activation of telomerase is the critical step for the immortalization of more than 90% of all human tumors.
source: Activation of telomerase is the critical step for the immortalization of more than 90% of all human tumors (Greider and Blackburn, 1985; Counter, 1992; Kim et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Non-coding mutations in the promoter of TERT emerged as one of the most prevalent mutations in human cancer.
source: Non-coding mutations in the promoter of the catalytic subunit of telomerase (TERT) emerged recently as one of the most prevalent mutations in human cancer (Bojesen et al., 2013; Horn et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2013; Killela et al., 2013; Fredriksson et al.,2014; Weinhold et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: All TERT promoter mutations associated with cancer formation generate novel binding sites for the ETS family of transcription factors.
source: Interestingly, all TERT promoter mutations associated with cancer formation thus far generate novel binding sites for the ETS (E26 transformation-specific) family of transcription factors and are located close to the translational start site of TERT (e.g., −57A/C, −124C/T, and −146C/T) (Horn et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: TERT promoter mutations can increase TERT transcription by 1.5–2 fold when assayed in tumor cells using transient transfection experiments with ectopic TERT Luciferase-reporter constructs.
source: Transient transfection experiments using ectopic TERT Luciferase-reporter constructs suggest that TERT promoter mutations can increase TERT transcription by 1.5–2 fold when assayed in tumor cells (Horn et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In untransformed human tissues, telomerase activity is restricted to embryonic cells and some adult stem cell or progenitor compartments due to transcriptional silencing of TERT upon differentiation.
source: In untransformed human tissues, telomerase activity is restricted to embryonic cells and some adult stem cell or progenitor compartments due to transcriptional silencing of TERT upon differentiation (Gunes and Rudolph, 2013; Aubert, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Differentiated somatic cells undergo progressive telomere shortening with cell division, which limits their proliferative capacity.
source: As a consequence, differentiated somatic cells undergo progressive telomere shortening with cell division, which limits their proliferative capacity and has thus been proposed as a tumor suppressor mechanism (Wright et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Critically short telomeres are detected as sites of DNA damage leading to cell death or replicative senescence.
source: Critically short telomeres are detected as sites of DNA damage leading to cell death or replicative senescence (Palm and de Lange, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Long-term inhibition of TERT leads to cell death in telomerase-positive cancer and stem cells.
source: Long-term inhibition of TERT (Herbert et al., 1999) or interference with telomerase recruitment to telomeres (Nakashima et al., 2013; Sexton et al., 2014) lead to cell death in telomerase-positive cancer and stem cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Ectopic telomerase expression is sufficient to immortalize normal human fibroblasts by allowing them to bypass senescence.
source: Inversely, ectopic telomerase expression is sufficient to immortalize normal human fibroblasts by allowing them to bypass senescence (Bodnar et al., 1998; Morales et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: TERT promoter mutations are bound predominantly by GABP.
source: While ETS-factors are a large family of transcription factors that can recognize this binding site, recent data suggest that TERT promoter mutations are bound predominantly by GABP (Bell et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TERT promoter mutations have been hypothesized to preferentially promote tumor progression in tissues with relatively low rates of self-renewal.
source: Based on this tumor spectrum, TERT promoter mutations have been hypothesized to preferentially promote tumor progression in tissues with relatively low rates of self-renewal (Killela et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TERT promoter mutations can provide a biomarker to stratify human cancer subtypes.
source: Several studies have suggested that TERT promoter mutations can provide a biomarker to stratify human cancer subtypes (Heidenreich et al., 2014; Borah et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The most prevalent TERT promoter mutation (−124C/T) resulted in a 2–3-fold increase in TERT expression compared to the isogenic wild-type control in hESCs.
source: This analysis revealed that the most frequent TERT mutation (−124C/T) resulted in a 2–3-fold increase in TERT expression when compared to the isogenic wild-type control.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The −57A/C and −146C/T TERT promoter mutations did not result in increased TERT expression in hESCs.
source: Noticeably, the two other mutations did not result in similarly increased TERT expression in hESCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The promoter mutation cell lines carrying the −124C/T mutation had elevated levels of TERT mRNA expression without an equivalent increase in telomerase activity.
source: Interestingly, the promoter mutation cell lines carrying the −124C/T mutation had elevated levels of TERT mRNA expression, without a equivalent increase in telomerase activity (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: TR overexpression strongly increased telomerase activity and led to rapid telomere elongation in hESCs.
source: TR overexpression strongly increased telomerase activity and led to rapid telomere elongation in hESCs, while overexpression of TERT alone did neither.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: Overexpression of TERT alone in hESCs did not increase telomerase activity or lead to telomere elongation.
source: TR overexpression strongly increased telomerase activity and led to rapid telomere elongation in hESCs, while overexpression of TERT alone did neither.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D and 2E.

claim: When hESCs were differentiated into fibroblasts or neural precursor cells, telomerase activity levels were significantly increased when TERT was overexpressed while increased levels of TR did not affect telomerase activity.
source: However, when differentiated into fibroblasts or neural precursor cells (NPCs), we observed the inverse behavior. In this setting, telomerase activity levels were significantly increased when TERT was overexpressed while increased levels of TR did not affect telomerase activity (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In hESCs, TERT levels are not limiting for telomerase activity.
source: This finding showed that in hESCs TERT levels were not limiting, and that increased TERT expression did not result in a significant increase of telomerase activity or telomere length.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from TERT and TR overexpression experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: TR, but not TERT, is limiting for telomerase activity in hESCs.
source: A lack of a significant change in telomerase activity despite increased TERT levels in hESCs that carry the −124C/T mutations suggested that TERT mRNA levels are not rate-limiting for telomerase activity in hESCs.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from overexpression experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: All three TERT promoter mutation lines retained significant levels of TERT expression during differentiation to embryonic bodies, while wild-type cells successfully down-regulated TERT expression.
source: Although TERT expression was successfully down-regulated in cells with wild-type TERT promoter, all three promoter mutation lines retained significant levels of TERT expression (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The failure of TERT transcriptional silencing in cells with promoter mutations became apparent as early as 3 days after the induction of differentiation.
source: This failure of TERT transcriptional silencing became apparent as early as 3 days after the induction of differentiation and accumulated into a fourfold increase in TERT expression in cells that carried the −57A/C or the −146C/T mutation and an 8–12-fold increase in cells in which transcription depended on the endogenous TERT promoter with the −124C/T mutation (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Cells with the −57A/C or −146C/T mutation showed a fourfold increase in TERT expression during differentiation.
source: This failure of TERT transcriptional silencing became apparent as early as 3 days after the induction of differentiation and accumulated into a fourfold increase in TERT expression in cells that carried the −57A/C or the −146C/T mutation and an 8–12-fold increase in cells in which transcription depended on the endogenous TERT promoter with the −124C/T mutation (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Cells with the −124C/T mutation showed an 8–12-fold increase in TERT expression during differentiation.
source: This failure of TERT transcriptional silencing became apparent as early as 3 days after the induction of differentiation and accumulated into a fourfold increase in TERT expression in cells that carried the −57A/C or the −146C/T mutation and an 8–12-fold increase in cells in which transcription depended on the endogenous TERT promoter with the −124C/T mutation (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: TERT transcription was undetectable in differentiated wild-type fibroblasts.
source: As expected, TERT transcription was undetectable in differentiated wild-type fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Fibroblasts with cancer-associated TERT promoter mutations showed high levels of TERT expression.
source: In contrast, fibroblasts with the cancer-associated promoter mutations showed high levels of TERT expression (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Telomerase activity is not detectable in wild-type fibroblasts.
source: Importantly, while telomerase activity is not detectable in wild-type fibroblasts, the aberrant TERT expression resulted in robust telomerase activity in fibroblasts that contained the promoter mutations (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Aberrant TERT expression resulted in robust telomerase activity in fibroblasts that contained the TERT promoter mutations.
source: Importantly, while telomerase activity is not detectable in wild-type fibroblasts, the aberrant TERT expression resulted in robust telomerase activity in fibroblasts that contained the promoter mutations (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The failure to repress TERT expression persists in fibroblasts as late as 45 days after differentiation.
source: Furthermore we confirmed that this failure to repress TERT expression persists in fibroblasts as late as 45 days after differentiation (Figures 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: All cells differentiated into NPCs and neurons with equal efficiency, showing equal down-regulation of OCT4 expression and induction of neuronal marker genes, independent of their genotype.
source: Independent of their genotype, all cells were able to differentiate into NPCs and neurons showing equal down-regulation of OCT4 expression and induction of neuronal marker genes (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: NPCs and neurons that carried the TERT promoter mutations failed to repress TERT transcription and showed robust telomerase activity.
source: However, a striking difference became apparent in TERT levels as both NPCs and neurons that carried the TERT promoter mutations failed to repress TERT transcription (Figure 4A,C and Figures 4—figure supplement 1) and showed robust telomerase activity (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A, 4C, 4D, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: When neurons were maintained in the presence of a mitotic inhibitor, the TERT promoter mutations led to elevated TERT mRNA and telomerase activity levels as late as 1 month after induction of terminal differentiation.
source: Even when neurons were maintained in the presence of a mitotic inhibitor, the promoter mutations led to elevated TERT mRNA and telomerase activity levels, suggesting that telomerase activity can accumulate in slowly and non-dividing cells as late as 1 month after induction of terminal differentiation (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and 4D.

claim: Telomerase activity levels in −124C/T NPCs were equivalent to the activity found in immortal Hela S3 cells and about 50% of the activity found in hESCs, HCT116, and 293T cells.
source: Remarkably, telomerase activity levels in −124C/T NPCs were equivalent to the activity found in immortal Hela S3 cells and about 50% of the activity found in hESCs, HCT116, and 293T cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: −124C/T fibroblasts had about 50% of the telomerase activity measured in HeLa S3 cells, 30% of that found in 293T cells, and 25% of that of HCT116 colon carcinoma cells.
source: Moreover, −124C/T fibroblasts had about 50% of the telomerase activity measured in HeLa S3 cells, 30% of that found in 293T cells, and 25% of that of HCT116 colon carcinoma cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: All differentiated cell lines with cancer-associated TERT promoter mutations showed an increase in telomere length compared to the wild-type controls.
source: All differentiated cell lines with cancer-associated promoter mutations showed an increase in telomere length compared to the wild-type controls.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, 5D, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: All cell lines injected formed teratomas of approximately equal size.
source: For this assay all cell lines were injected subcutaneously into NOD/SCID mice, allowing pluripotent cells to differentiate and form a teratoma comprised of cells derived from all three germ layers. All cell lines injected formed teratomas of approximately equal size, were explanted simultaneously (75 days after injection), and analyzed for their telomere length.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from teratoma formation assays.

claim: Cells with TERT promoter mutations in teratomas carried aberrantly long telomeres.
source: Using this unbiased approach, we again found that cells with TERT promoter mutations carried aberrantly long telomeres, with the −124C/T mutation having the strongest defect in silencing telomerase activity and retaining almost identical telomere length as undifferentiated hESCs (Figure 5C,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, 5E, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The −124C/T mutation had the strongest defect in silencing telomerase activity in teratomas and retained almost identical telomere length as undifferentiated hESCs.
source: Using this unbiased approach, we again found that cells with TERT promoter mutations carried aberrantly long telomeres, with the −124C/T mutation having the strongest defect in silencing telomerase activity and retaining almost identical telomere length as undifferentiated hESCs (Figure 5C,E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C, 5E, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TERT promoter mutations can up-regulate TERT levels sufficiently to suppress telomere erosion without additional tumor-selected changes.
source: These data demonstrated the causal relationship between the TERT promoter mutations and telomere maintenance and showed that the TERT promoter mutations can up-regulate TERT levels sufficiently to suppress telomere erosion without additional tumor-selected changes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from teratoma experiments showing telomere maintenance in cells with TERT promoter mutations.

claim: The −57A/C and −146C/T mutations generate the same putative ETS-binding motif of TTCCGG as the −124C/T mutation.
source: However, neither the −57A/C nor the −146C/T mutation led to an increase in TERT transcription, despite the fact that these mutations generate the same putative ETS-binding motif of TTCCGG.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the sequence changes introduced by the mutations.

claim: There is a strong positional effect between the location of the ETS mutation and the core transcription initiation machinery.
source: This suggests a strong positional effect between the location of the ETS mutation and the core transcription initiation machinery.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that different mutations creating the same ETS motif have different effects on TERT expression depending on their position.

claim: A single point mutation at position −89 (C/G) would result in the same TTCCGG sequence but has not been reported to be associated with cancer.
source: The possibility of such context-dependent positional constraints between the TERT promoter mutations and the core transcriptional machinery is further supported by the fact that a single point mutation at position −89 (C/G, −31 bp upstream of the TSS) would result in the same TTCCGG sequence. The fact that this mutation has as of now not been reported to be associated with cancer despite it being between the −57 and −124 sites is likely due to the need of the core transcription factors to bind to this site.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the absence of this mutation in cancer databases and knowledge of the sequence.

claim: The underlying cancer-causing mechanism of TERT promoter mutations is likely a failure to repress telomerase upon differentiation into somatic cells.
source: These experiments uncover that the underlying cancer-causing mechanism is likely a failure to repress telomerase upon differentiation into somatic cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that TERT promoter mutations prevent silencing of TERT during differentiation.

claim: TERT promoter mutations are sufficient to up-regulate TERT expression without additional cancer-selected changes in the genome such as increased levels of ETS factors.
source: It is remarkable that TERT promoter mutations are sufficient to up-regulate TERT expression without additional cancer-selected changes in the genome such as increased levels of ETS factors.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental design using genome-edited cells with only the TERT promoter mutations in an otherwise wild-type background.

claim: TERT promoter mutations are not frequently found in leukemias and colorectal cancers.
source: TERT promoter mutations are not frequently found in leukemias and colorectal cancers (Heidenreich et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: TERT is expressed in highly proliferative tissues such as bone marrow, lung, intestine, and skin and is required for their long-term self-renewal capacity and ability to maintain tissue homeostasis.
source: Direct evidence (Chiu et al., 1996; Schepers et al., 2011) as well as the pathology of the telomerase-related disease dyskeratosis congenita in which patients with mutations in the telomere maintenance pathway present with bone marrow failure as well as lung, intestinal, and skin pathologies show that TERT is expressed in these highly proliferative tissues and is required for their long-term self-renewal capacity and ability to maintain tissue homeostasis (Armanios and Price, 2012; Aubert et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In tissues with telomerase-positive stem cells, mutations in the TERT promoter might be neutral at first, not providing a direct proliferative advantage as telomeres are still long or telomerase is active.
source: In this setting, mutations in the TERT promoter or alterations in the telomerase biogenesis pathway might be at first neutral, not providing a direct proliferative advantage as telomeres are still long or telomerase is active (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model presented in the manuscript.

claim: In telomerase-negative cells with short telomeres, a cell acquiring a TERT promoter mutation can bypass the Hayflick limit, immortalize, and outcompete its neighboring cells.
source: In contrast, a cell with short telomeres acquiring a TERT promoter mutation can bypass the Hayflick limit (dashed lines), immortalize, and outcompete its neighboring cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model presented in the manuscript and supported by experimental data.

claim: TERT promoter mutations will provide an immediate and strong proliferative advantage over neighboring cells in tumor-initiating cells that undergo high numbers of divisions after differentiating or that have to reenter a proliferation cycle in response to chronic injury.
source: In contrast, tumor-initiating cells that are thought to not directly arise from a canonical telomerase-positive stem cell compartment (e.g., liposarcomas), that undergo high numbers of divisions after differentiating (e.g., neural-crest derived melanocytes), or that have to reenter a proliferation cycle in response to chronic injury (e.g., urothelial cells and hepatocytes) could be challenged by the telomere-dependent proliferative barrier comparatively early in their progression. In these cell types TERT promoter mutations will provide an immediate and strong proliferative advantage over neighboring cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model and supported by the tumor spectrum data.

claim: Telomerase inhibition has been proposed as a target for cancer therapies.
source: Telomerase inhibition has been proposed as a target for cancer therapies.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge in the field.

claim: TERT promoter mutations are exclusive to tumor cells and are not present in surrounding normal tissue.
source: Specifically targeting the TERT promoter mutations is an attractive approach, as TERT promoter mutations are exclusive to the tumor cells and are not present in surrounding normal tissue.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the somatic nature of these mutations in cancer.

claim: Any intervention that is targeted specifically against TERT promoter mutations is expected to affect tumor cell survival, but not the telomerase-positive adult stem cells of the patient.
source: Therefore, any intervention that is targeted specifically against their mode of operation is expected to affect tumor cell survival, but not the telomerase-positive adult stem cells of the patient.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the specificity of TERT promoter mutations to tumor cells.

claim: TERTΔ/Δ hESCs are telomerase-negative.
source: As the first deletion step removed the translational start site as well as some coding sequence of TERT, this targeting strategy resulted in telomerase-negative hESCs (TERTΔ/Δ) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: TERTΔ/Δ hESCs proliferated normally for 3 to 4 months, followed by cell death due to progressive telomere shortening with no survivors after 140 days.
source: As expected from our previous characterization of TERT−/− hESCs (Sexton et al., 2014), these cells proliferated normally for 3 to 4 months, followed by cell death due to progressive telomere shortening with no survivors after 140 days (Sexton et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and a citation to prior work.

claim: Cells with a restored TERT gene gradually outcompeted none-rescued parental TERTΔ/Δ cells and lead to substantial telomere elongation by the time untargeted TERTΔ/Δ hESCs had died.
source: Accordingly, cells with a restored TERT gene gradually outcompeted none-rescued parental TERTΔ/Δ cells and lead to substantial telomere elongation by the time untargeted TERTΔ/Δ hESCs had died (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The complementation strategy successfully generated hESCs that differed exclusively at the TERT locus by expressing TERT either from its wild-type promoter or from a promoter that contained one of the cancer-associated point mutations.
source: This complementation strategy therefore successfully generated hESCs that differed exclusively at the TERT locus by expressing TERT either from its wild-type promoter or from a promoter that contained one of the cancer-associated point mutations.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental design and validation data.

claim: The increase in TERT expression from the −124C/T mutation is in agreement with previous reports that evaluated these mutations using Luciferase reporter constructs.
source: This increase is in agreement with previous reports that evaluated these mutations using Luciferase reporter constructs (Horn et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature and comparison with current data.

claim: Telomerase activity is limited by levels of TR in some tumor cell lines.
source: Similar observations were made previously for some tumor cell lines in which telomerase activity is limited by levels of TR (Cristofari and Lingner, 2006; Xu and Blackburn, 2007), and might explain the tissue-specific impact of TERT and TR mutations in patients with dyskeratosis congenita (Batista et al., 2011; Strong et al., 2011; Armanios and Blackburn, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Telomerase biogenesis is a complex biological process that has been shown in human pluripotent stem cells to depend on several activities that, when depleted, can become limiting.
source: Telomerase biogenesis is a complex biological process that has been shown in human pluripotent stem cells to depend on several activities that, when depleted, can become limiting (Yang et al., 2008; Batista et al., 2011; Batista and Artandi, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: TERT mRNA was overexpressed >40 fold in TERT overexpression cell lines.
source: Overexpression levels were verified by western and northern blotting and qRT-PCR (Figure 2B,C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) and quantitative analysis showed that TERT mRNA was overexpressed >40 fold and TR levels by approximately 20 fold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, 2C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TR levels were overexpressed by approximately 20 fold in TR overexpression cell lines.
source: Overexpression levels were verified by western and northern blotting and qRT-PCR (Figure 2B,C; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) and quantitative analysis showed that TERT mRNA was overexpressed >40 fold and TR levels by approximately 20 fold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B, 2C, and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TERT protein was detectable by immunoblotting when overexpressed, contrasted to the lack of detectable endogenous TERT protein.
source: TERT protein was detectable by immunoblotting when overexpressed, contrasted to the lack of detectable endogenous TERT protein.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: All cell lines differentiated with equal efficiencies, as evidenced by up-regulation of the differentiation marker COL1A1 and repression of OCT4 transcription.
source: All cell lines differentiated with equal efficiencies, as evidenced by up-regulation of the differentiation marker COL1A1 and repression of OCT4 transcription (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B and 3C.

claim: The difference in TERT expression between wild-type and mutant cells was not due to impaired differentiation of cells with the TERT promoter mutations, as these cells had silenced OCT4 and appropriately induced COL1A1 expression.
source: This difference was not due to impaired differentiation of cells with the TERT promoter mutations, as these cells had silenced OCT4 and appropriately induced COL1A1 expression (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The failure to appropriately repress TERT transcription during EB differentiation became even more apparent when the cells were differentiated into fibroblast-like cells.
source: This failure to appropriately repress TERT transcription during EB differentiation became even more apparent when the cells were differentiated into fibroblast-like cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing TERT expression in EBs versus fibroblasts.

claim: The failure to silence telomerase could be specific to the fibroblast differentiation paradigm or a more general defect during differentiation.
source: The failure to silence telomerase could be specific to the fibroblast differentiation paradigm or a more general defect during differentiation.
evidence: This is a question posed by the authors that they address experimentally.

claim: NPCs can be maintained in culture for extended periods of time with low levels of telomerase expression.
source: To address this issue, we first generated NPCs using the highly robust dual SMAD inhibition protocol (Chambers et al., 2009), establishing NPCs that can be maintained in culture for extended periods of time with low levels of telomerase expression.
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental design and citation to the differentiation protocol.

claim: NPCs can be further differentiated towards terminally differentiated non-proliferating post mitotic neurons that are characterized by the expression of the pan-neural marker proteins TUJ1 and NEUN.
source: These NPCs can be further differentiated towards terminally differentiated non-proliferating post mitotic neurons that are characterized by the expression of the pan-neural marker proteins TUJ1 and NEUN.
evidence: This claim is based on the experimental design and characterization of differentiated neurons.

claim: TERT promoter mutations induce telomerase levels that are sufficient to enable immortalization or at least significantly delay telomere length-induced senescence.
source: These findings suggested that TERT promoter mutations induce telomerase levels that are sufficient to enable immortalization or at least significantly delay telomere length-induced senescence.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of telomerase activity levels in mutant cells to those in immortal cancer cell lines.

claim: Cells with TERT promoter mutations were assayed for teratoma tumor formation in immune-compromised mice.
source: To further explore the in vivo relevance of these findings in the context of long-term differentiation as well as tumor progression, cells with TERT promoter mutations were assayed for teratoma tumor formation in immune-compromised mice (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental approach used.

claim: All cell lines injected formed teratomas comprised of cells derived from all three germ layers.
source: For this assay all cell lines were injected subcutaneously into NOD/SCID mice, allowing pluripotent cells to differentiate and form a teratoma comprised of cells derived from all three germ layers.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental approach and expected outcome.

claim: The data demonstrated the causal relationship between the TERT promoter mutations and telomere maintenance.
source: These data demonstrated the causal relationship between the TERT promoter mutations and telomere maintenance and showed that the TERT promoter mutations can up-regulate TERT levels sufficiently to suppress telomere erosion without additional tumor-selected changes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that only the TERT promoter mutations are responsible for the observed phenotype.

claim: Genome editing of the endogenous TERT locus generated a panel of three hESC lines that differed exclusively at a single position in the TERT promoter associated with cancer.
source: Using genome editing of the endogenous TERT locus we generated a panel of three hESC lines that differed exclusively at a single position in the TERT promoter associated with cancer.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental approach and outcome.

claim: The most frequent mutation, −124C/T, increased TERT mRNA levels in hESCs by about 2–3 fold.
source: Analyzing the impact of these mutations in hESCs, we showed that the most frequent mutation, −124C/T, increased TERT mRNA levels in hESCs by about 2–3 fold.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Neither the −57A/C nor the −146C/T mutation led to an increase in TERT transcription in hESCs.
source: However, neither the −57A/C nor the −146C/T mutation led to an increase in TERT transcription, despite the fact that these mutations generate the same putative ETS-binding motif of TTCCGG.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The experimental approach of genome editing the TERT promoter provides an experimental system to uncover cis-regulatory elements that are necessary for telomerase expression in stem cells and its transcriptional regulation upon differentiation.
source: The experimental approach established in this study of genome editing the TERT promoter provides an experimental system to uncover cis-regulatory elements that are necessary for telomerase expression in stem cells and its transcriptional regulation upon differentiation.
evidence: This claim describes the utility of the experimental system developed.

claim: Immortal hESCs are as uninformative with regard to cancer-associated TERT mutations as immortal tumor tissue or cell lines.
source: Therefore, immortal hESCs are as uninformative with regard to cancer-associated TERT mutations as immortal tumor tissue or cell lines.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that TERT is not limiting in hESCs.

claim: Whereas upon differentiation wild-type hESCs efficiently silence TERT transcription, resulting in loss of telomerase activity and telomere shortening, the cancer-associated TERT promoter mutations were sufficient to maintain expression of TERT and resulted in telomerase activity levels comparable to immortal cancer cell lines.
source: However, whereas upon differentiation wild-type hESCs efficiently silence TERT transcription, resulting in loss of telomerase activity and telomere shortening, the cancer-associated TERT promoter mutations were sufficient to maintain expression of TERT and resulted in telomerase activity levels comparable to immortal cancer cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3, 4, and 5.

claim: TERT is expressed in highly proliferative tissues such as hematopoietic and intestinal systems and is required for their long-term self-renewal capacity.
source: Direct evidence (Chiu et al., 1996; Schepers et al., 2011) as well as the pathology of the telomerase-related disease dyskeratosis congenita in which patients with mutations in the telomere maintenance pathway present with bone marrow failure as well as lung, intestinal, and skin pathologies show that TERT is expressed in these highly proliferative tissues and is required for their long-term self-renewal capacity and ability to maintain tissue homeostasis (Armanios and Price, 2012; Aubert et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Tumor-initiating events in cancers with telomerase-positive stem cells predominantly drive proliferation pathways that spur formation of hyperplasia and niche-independent proliferation that allow incipient cancer cells to outcompete their neighbors.
source: Tumor-initiating events in these cancers predominantly drive proliferation pathways that spur formation of hyperplasia and niche-independent proliferation that allow incipient cancer cells to outcompete their neighbors (Barker et al., 2009; Zhou et al., 2009; Merlos-Suarez et al., 2011; Magee et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In tissues with telomerase-positive stem cells, mutations in the TERT promoter or alterations in the telomerase biogenesis pathway might be at first neutral, not providing a direct proliferative advantage as telomeres are still long or telomerase is active.
source: In this setting, mutations in the TERT promoter or alterations in the telomerase biogenesis pathway might be at first neutral, not providing a direct proliferative advantage as telomeres are still long or telomerase is active (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is based on inference and speculation from the model presented.

claim: During the genesis of tumors from telomerase-positive stem cells, telomere shortening might present a challenge at a later stage when cells have already outcompeted their neighbors.
source: During the genesis of these tumors, telomere shortening might present a challenge at a later stage when cells have already outcompeted their neighbors.
evidence: This claim is based on inference and speculation from the model presented.

claim: In telomerase-negative differentiated cells with short telomeres, a proliferation-promoting mutation will provide a growth advantage but these cells will enter replicative senescence or die.
source: A proliferation-promoting mutation will also provide a growth advantage in telomerase-negative differentiated cells with short telomeres, however, these cells will enter replicative senescence or die.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model presented in Figure 6B.

claim: In tumor-initiating cells that undergo high numbers of divisions after differentiating or that have to reenter a proliferation cycle in response to chronic injury, telomerase activation occurs in cells in which telomerase is absent or low and which have an otherwise mostly intact genome.
source: In this case telomerase activation occurs in cells in which telomerase is absent or low and which have an otherwise mostly intact genome.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model and tumor spectrum data.

claim: In cells where telomerase activation occurs early, activating TERT promoter mutations will be present in most tumor cells and detected as a frequent and thus early event.
source: In these cells activating TERT promoter mutations will be present in most tumor cells and detected as a frequent and thus early event (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the model presented.

claim: The sharp distinction between canonical telomerase-positive stem cell compartments and telomerase-negative compartments is rather continuous in vivo.
source: It is important to note that this model depicts the very extreme cases of a TERT-positive adult stem cell with long telomeres contrasted to the expected outcome of a TERT promoter mutation in a telomerase-negative cell with short telomeres. Likely this sharp distinction between canonical telomerase-positive stem cell compartments and telomerase-negative compartments is rather continuous in vivo.
evidence: This claim is based on inference and speculation about the complexity of in vivo biology.

claim: Telomerase expression, telomere length, and the number of cell divisions will differ between tissues and with age and therefore the benefit of the TERT promoter mutation will be complexly graded.
source: Telomerase expression, telomere length, and the number of cell divisions will differ between tissues and with age and therefore the benefit of the TERT promoter mutation will be complexly graded.
evidence: This claim is based on inference and speculation about tissue-specific differences.

claim: It will be critical to determine exactly which cells of the human body are telomerase-positive, when and how telomerase is silenced upon differentiation, and how many divisions cells undergo in human tissue after becoming telomerase-negative.
source: Given this, it will be critical to determine exactly which cells of the human body are telomerase-positive, when and how telomerase is silenced upon differentiation, and how many divisions cells undergo in human tissue after becoming telomerase-negative.
evidence: This claim represents a future research direction identified by the authors.

claim: TERT promoter mutations provide a potential target to inhibit TERT expression and telomerase activity.
source: We demonstrate that TERT promoter mutations are sufficient to de-repress TERT, providing a potential target to inhibit TERT expression and telomerase activity.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the experimental findings.

claim: A model system in which TERT is dysregulated solely by TERT promoter mutations is necessary to identify therapeutic approaches specific to these promoter mutations.
source: In order to identify therapeutic approaches specific to these promoter mutations, a model system in which TERT is dysregulated solely by these mutations is necessary.
evidence: This claim is based on inference about the requirements for therapeutic development.

claim: The model system developed fulfills the requirement of having TERT dysregulated solely by TERT promoter mutations and allows for a direct assessment of any potential inhibition by measuring TERT expression following differentiation.
source: Our model system fulfills this requirement and allows for a direct assessment of any potential inhibition by measuring TERT expression following differentiation.
evidence: This claim describes the utility of the experimental system developed.

claim: Evaluating the effectiveness of TERT inhibitors in tumor cells is challenging due to the high frequency of concurrent TERT copy number variations, promoter polymorphisms, and cancer-associated dysregulation of factors implicated in TERT regulation such as MYC.
source: In contrast, this approach will be challenging in cancer cells, as TERT mRNA levels, telomerase levels, and telomere length vary dramatically regardless of whether they carry any of the TERT promoter mutations. Further mechanistic studies in such tumor cells are also challenged by the high frequency of concurrent TERT copy number variations, promoter polymorphisms, and cancer-associated dysregulation of factors implicated in TERT regulation such as MYC.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the complexity of cancer cell genomes.

claim: It is imperative to test any potential therapeutic approach directed at TERT promoter mutations in a model system that only carries these mutations in an otherwise wild-type background.
source: As such, it is imperative to test any potential therapeutic approach directed at these promoter mutations in a model system that only carries these mutations in an otherwise wild-type background, such as the model system described here.
evidence: This claim is based on inference about the requirements for therapeutic testing.

claim: Specifically targeting the TERT promoter mutations is an attractive approach because TERT promoter mutations are exclusive to the tumor cells and are not present in surrounding normal tissue.
source: Specifically targeting the TERT promoter mutations is an attractive approach, as TERT promoter mutations are exclusive to the tumor cells and are not present in surrounding normal tissue.
evidence: This claim is based on knowledge of the somatic nature of these mutations.

claim: Any intervention that is targeted specifically against TERT promoter mutations is expected to affect tumor cell survival, but not the telomerase-positive adult stem cells of the patient.
source: Therefore, any intervention that is targeted specifically against their mode of operation is expected to affect tumor cell survival, but not the telomerase-positive adult stem cells of the patient.
